terms.meaning: The famous army of the Badami Chalukyas.
A district in the Chalukya kingdom, run by a vishayadhipati.
A three-line Kannada verse form that began in this period.
The Chalukya style of temple architecture.
Nayannars: 63 saints of the Shaiva faith. Alwars: 12 saints of the Vaishnava faith.

items.name: Founder of the Badami Chalukyas
items.example: They ruled for about 200 years, from the 6th to the mid 8th century.

items.name: Pulakeshi II's victories
items.formula: Defeated the Gangas, Kadambas, Alupas and the Pallava Mahendravarma; stopped Harsha at the Narmada.
items.example: Titles: Dakshinapatheshwara, Lord of the Peninsula.

items.name: Chalukyas of Vengi
items.formula: Pulakeshi II made his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana head of Vengi.
items.example: That branch ruled for about five centuries.

items.name: Foreign views of Pulakeshi II
items.formula: Hiuen Tsang praised his just rule and brave army.
items.example: Arab historians say he had ties with the Persian king Khusru II.

items.name: End of the Badami Chalukyas
items.formula: Narasimhavarma I took Vatapi to avenge his father.
items.example: Under the last king Kirtivarma, the Rashtrakutas took over.

items.name: Literature under the Badami Chalukyas
items.formula: Kannada was the state language; Kappe Arabhatta's inscription has a tripadi.

items.name: Chalukya temples
items.formula: Aihole was a cradle of temple building; the style matured at Pattadakallu (Virupaksha, Mallikarjuna).
items.example: Badami caves have Vishnu, Varaha, Harihara and Ardhanarishwara.

items.name: Beginning and end of the Pallavas
items.formula: First kings of Tamil Nadu, once officials of the Shatavahanas; first king Shivaskandavarma.
items.example: Aditya Chola ended their rule under Aparajita.

items.name: Narasimhavarma I
items.formula: Most famous Pallava: beat Pulakeshi II, took Vatapi, titles Mahamalla and Vatapikonda.
items.example: He built Mahabalipuram, a city on the coast near Kanchi.

items.name: Pallava administration
items.formula: Kingdom in mandala, nadu and grama.
items.example: The gramasabha handled village problems and the gramabhojaka ran the village.

items.name: Pallava literature
items.example: Mahendravarma wrote Matta Vilasa Prahasana and Bhagavadajjukam.

items.name: Pallava temples
items.formula: Monolithic Pancharathas and the "Arjuna's Meditation" carving at Mahabalipuram.
items.example: At Kanchi: Kailasanath, Ekambarnath and Vaikunta Perumal.

mistakes.text: Pulakeshi II beat Mahendravarma; then Mahendravarma's son Narasimhavarma I beat Pulakeshi II.
Vijjika, who wrote Kaumudi Mahotsav, was Pulakeshi II's daughter-in-law, not his daughter.
63 Nayannars were Shaiva; 12 Alwars were Vaishnava.
